series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Argentina shall not exceed a net emission of 483 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2eq) by the year 2030.The goal shall be achieved through several implementation means throughout the economy, focusing on energy sectors, agriculture, forests, transport, industry and waste. " "Argentina has also calculated the impact of conditional measures, which if jointly implemented could bring emissions to 369 million tCO2eq for 2030. These measures don't integrate the contribution, but define a future work which shall advance together with international community in order to solve the aspects that lay the foundation of its conditionality in order to include them in a new NDC to be presented in the future. The conditionality of the measures have several origins and can be briefed in aspects referred to: a) international funding; b)the support to the transference, innovation and development of technologies (for example; to accurately measure and monitor the reductions and captures obtained); c) the support to the creation of capacities to spread good practices and effectively implement the proposed measures. If all conditional measures were implemented jointly to the unconditional ones, Argentina would reduce a total of 223 million tCO2eq with respect to the 2030 baseline scenario." Argentina NDC also includes an adaptation component.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: Not exceed a net emission of 483 (unconditional) million tCO2eq by the year 2030; conditional measures, if jointly implemented could bring emissions to 369 million tCO2eq for 2030.
ndc_assessment.gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6
ndc_assessment.sectors: Energy, industrial processes, agriculture, cattle, land use change, silviculture and waste

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is Second NDC (Updated submission), filed 2021-11-02. 52 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (6). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 417 MtCO₂e, DS-02 394.4 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 2 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 50.4 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: Not exceed a net emission of 483 (unconditional) million tCO2eq by the year 2030; conditional measures, if jointly implemented could bring emissions to 369 million tCO2eq for 2030. It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +0.88°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.54°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
